claims.explanation: Buphenine is a beta-adrenergic agonist whose only annotated target is ADRB2, so selective killing most plausibly reflects dependence on ADRB2 signaling or on the downstream cAMP/PKA pathway that beta-agonists engage. Lines with high ADRB2 expression and intact Gs-cAMP signaling (e.g., EGFR-mutant or BRAF-mutant lung, gastric, and melanoma lines) are sensitized, while lines with low ADRB2 or with lesions that blunt cAMP signaling (e.g., high phosphodiesterase activity, GNAS/PDE mutations, or neuroendocrine/squamous phenotypes) are protected. The pattern is not explained by any single driver mutation, so expression of the receptor and its signaling axis is the strongest predictor.
